title: The Cold War
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:52Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches the whole Cold War as the brief describes it, and the closest ones cover only its origins or its end, at Year 12 depth rather than Year 10.

draft.title: The Cold War
card: After 1945 the United States and the Soviet Union became rival superpowers. Each led a group of allies and tried to spread its own way of running a country.
It was called a cold war because the two did not fight each other directly. Tension stayed high, and each side feared the other's nuclear weapons.
The rivals competed in other ways, such as building weapons, backing allies in wars in other countries, and racing into space.
The Cold War ended when the Soviet Union broke up in 1991.
draft.remember: The Cold War was a rivalry between two superpowers that never became direct war between them.

a.q: Why was the Cold War called a cold war?
opts: The two superpowers did not fight each other directly
The main fighting took place in freezing regions
Neither side had any weapons to fight with
Both sides agreed to stop competing in 1945
a.why: The United States and the Soviet Union competed fiercely but did not fight each other directly. They did have large weapons stockpiles, so having no weapons is wrong.

b.q: A superpower sends weapons and money to an ally fighting a war in another country, rather than sending its own army against its rival. What does this show about the Cold War?
opts: Rivals competed without fighting each other directly
The two rivals had already ended their competition
The rivals were fighting a direct war
Only one superpower wanted influence abroad
b.why: Backing an ally in a war elsewhere let a superpower compete for influence without fighting its rival directly. A direct war would involve their own armies fighting each other.
b.clue: Who is actually fighting the rival's forces?

a.best: The two superpowers did not fight each other directly

b.best: Rivals competed without fighting each other directly
